items.title: How MasterClass Builds Multi-Agent AI That Learners Can Trust
items.summary: Students perform better when given more personalized opportunities to learn. But scaling personalized learning has always proven to be challenging. Teachers are limited, students are many, time is finite – until now. AI agents are the first technology that give us a shot at shifting this equation in favor of the learner. MasterClass will share how AI now runs through our learning products, and how we made a multi-agent system reliable enough to put in front of real learners. The talk covers our observability stack on CoreWeave: full tracing of every agent step, an MCP server that exposes those traces back to agents, and the AgentOps loop that lets our system diagnose and improve itself. Where AI sits across MasterClass products today, and the bet behind going multi-agent Why learning raises the reliability bar — the failure modes that matter most when a learner is on the other end Tracing on CoreWeave: end-to-end visibility into multi-agent runs, and the failure taxonomy that emerged AgentOps in practice — agents querying traces via MCP to root-cause, cluster, and build datasets from real usage

items.title: Beyond Faster Simulation: Hitting NASA's 2030 CFD Benchmark and the Infrastructure for Physics AI
items.summary: AI has drastically reduced the cost of producing software code, transforming early prototypes into inexpensive "price checks" rather than lengthy debates. However, engineering teams are still limited by the high cost of simulations and the fragility of geometry workflows in hardware. In 2015, NASA’s CFD Vision 2030 study issued a significant challenge: enabling a single engineer to run and interpret 10,000 simulations in 24 hours without manual intervention. This turns out to be a dual challenge: 1) harnessing enough computing power at a reasonable cost, and 2) generating CAD boundaries and body-fitting meshing that does not break under parametric variation or require human intervention. In this talk, we will explain how nTop and CoreWeave surpassed NASA’s 2030 milestone four years ahead of schedule. They completed 10,000 Large Eddy Simulation (LES) CFD runs in just 32.2 hours. This was done across a drone platform design space comprising 2,400 variants. By combining nTop’s robust implicit geometry engine with a GPU-native Lattice Boltzmann (LBM) solver, we eliminated geometry failures and meshing steps entirely. A single engineer deployed a lights-out pipeline running across 280 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs on CoreWeave that sustained near 100% compute utilization without any interventions during the run. Finally, we will demonstrate how generating 14 TB of structured 3D flow data can transform CFD from a late-stage validation tool into the primary training engine for real-time physics AI surrogates operating in implicit latent space.

items.title: Post-Training at the Frontier: How You.com, NVIDIA, and CoreWeave Improved Nemotron’s Agentic Search
items.summary: In this session, You.com’s engineering team will share their work with Nvidia and CoreWeave to post-train Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning on CoreWeave using Dynamo RL rollouts in NeMo gym with You.com’s web search API. We’ll walk through the technical approach, which enabled the team to rapidly iterate and drive measurable gains on BrowseComp, a benchmark for agentic web search and browsing. We will cover topics ranging from dataset preparation, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning to CoreWeave’s infrastructure for post-training. We’ll end with a blueprint for post-training and improving LLMs on real-world search tasks as well as a look at what’s next.

items.title: Systems of Record, Content & Intelligence: Where AI Fits in Enterprise Architecture
items.summary: Before you can talk about where AI adds value, you need to know which layer of the enterprise you are talking about. CRM for customers, ERP for financials, HR systems for employees. - System of Content: where unstructured content lives. Documents, emails, reports, contracts. Valuable, but harder to query and act on. - System of Intelligence: the AI and analytics layer sitting on top of both. It does not store data, it makes data useful. - AI Maturity: a framework for assessing how developed each layer is, and how effectively AI is applied across the organization Most organizations do not have all three working well at once. items.title: Quota Isn't Enough: Topology Aware Scheduling on Modern GPU Clusters
items.summary: Rack-scale systems are here! Fragmentation is widening the gap between “I have GPU quota” and “my job is actually running.” NVLink domains, rack boundaries, and the physical layout of the data center now shape whether a large training job can start, where it lands, and how efficiently it runs. On modern GPU clusters, quota is no longer enough. Topology has become a scheduling requirement. Kueue’s Topology Aware Scheduling (TAS) brings that reality into Kubernetes. In this session, you’ll learn how TAS works and the configuration choices that matter, including preferred versus required topologies and PodSet slices. You’ll also discover how topology-aware placement affects workload performance. Finally, you’ll walk away with the production lessons that do not show up in the happy path: sticky scheduling, quota debugging, fragmentation, and node hot swaps. Join us to understand how topology-aware scheduling helps AI teams turn expensive GPU capacity into actual training progress.
